answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a small refundable deposit in a shared escrow kernel before it may transact. The deposit is not a fee: honest agents get it back, while a detected duplicate forfeits it, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes linearly expensive. A lightweight cipher challenge binds each deposit to one hardware-backed key, and peer attestations act like an ember that only stays lit while the identity keeps doing useful, verifiable work. Dormant sockpuppets cool off and lose their deposit, while genuine agents keep earning.
